Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one original wide horizontal README orientation illustration, target 1920 by 640 pixels, approximately 3:1. Calm, publication-quality hand-drawn paper-and-marker style: pure white paper, slightly irregular dark navy pen outlines, large readable handwritten headings, indigo #3949AB and blue #1E69D6, soft light-blue and lavender washes, restrained purple, generous whitespace. Recognizable semantic objects rather than architecture boxes. This should match the GitHub Manager illustrated explainers and simple README banners.
Composition: three independent large vignettes across one row, with no enclosing panels, NO arrows and NO numbered sequence. These are subjects covered by an article, not one mandatory processing sequence. LEFT: an open README document with a highlighted passage, a small parsing tool/pencil, and two extracted paper slips visibly marked "E0" and "E1". Heading below exactly "Evidence Parser". CENTER: a magnifying glass over an open approved-label ledger, with two clean rounded label cards beside it, conveying local search over canonical label definitions. Heading below exactly "Canonical Retriever". RIGHT: a small friendly model robot beside a request booklet and two distinct outputs: a branching taxonomy sketch and selected rounded label cards with a small review check clipboard. Heading below exactly "Taxonomy & classification", split to two lines if necessary.
No text except those three headings and the two source-slip marks E0 and E1. No fake metrics, no formula, no dense fine print, no repeated overall title, no logos or watermark. All objects and lettering must remain clear at 850px display width. Keep ample edge margins and white space. The right vignette previews two related tasks; do not imply that taxonomy discovery retrieves canonical labels or that a model approves its own taxonomy.

figures.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one original friendly hand-drawn technical explainer, landscape 16:9, target 1920x1080. Audience: readers who want to understand what kind of retrieval-augmented generation GitHub Manager actually implements. Pure white paper, slightly irregular dark navy ink, clear large handwritten text, indigo #3949AB and blue #1E69D6 headings, soft light-blue and lavender marker washes, restrained purple for review. Generous whitespace, recognizable illustrated objects rather than generic service boxes. Clean readable publication style.
Title at top exactly "Our RAG approach".
Subtitle exactly "Fixed, single-pass retrieval-augmented classification".
Small supporting descriptor directly below: "Sparse label retrieval + durable application memory".
MAIN STORY: four clearly numbered illustrated stops left to right, with slender arrows between them. Use short exact labels and large objects.
1. Heading "Retrieve". Show small source evidence sheets marked "E0 + README" directed as a query toward a magnifying glass over an open canonical-label ledger. Ledger label exactly "Approved label definitions". Small algorithm caption "TF-IDF + alias boost". The retrieved objects are label cards, not README chunks or other repositories.
2. Heading "Augment". Show an open request booklet with three clearly separated inserts, labeled exactly "Compact evidence", "RAKE phrases", "Candidate definitions". Add a small system-instruction/schema tab labeled "Instructions + schema". A small incoming arrow from step 1 label cards joins this booklet; do not imply RAKE phrases are the retrieval query.
3. Heading "Generate". A friendly small model robot reading the booklet and returning a compact card labeled exactly "Canonical IDs + citations". The output is structured label selection, not an essay.
4. Heading "Validate & review". A local validation clipboard followed by a friendly human reviewer and a few suggestion chips; caption exactly "Reviewable suggestions". Never show automatic unquestioned approval or guaranteed correctness.
BOTTOM: a separate quiet illustrated shelf with saved profile papers, a taxonomy ledger, decision cards and analysis receipts. Heading exactly "Local application memory". One short caption exactly "Profiles · taxonomy · decisions · receipts". Do NOT draw an arrow looping from the model into retrieval, and do not show all stored history going into the model request. This shelf signifies persistent application state and avoiding repeat work, not a conversational/vector-memory retriever.
A small separate margin note at the bottom right, with a tiny vocabulary-tree sketch: "Taxonomy discovery proposes vocabulary separately". Keep it clearly outside the classification sequence.
Constraints: no embeddings, vector database, dense search, neural reranker, agentic tool loop or adaptive retrieval router. No fake scores or benchmark claims. The main flow must read clearly at 1000px display width. All text must be legible, accurately spelled and kept inside generous margins; no watermark.
